author: opt-N8

contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside: bracket reduction, 2 per pass plus init, tie phase under prefer_smaller_index (B1_n6b's code, unchanged)
contract.k_range: [1, N) at run time, measured k 16, 64, 256
contract.n_range: N = Threads x IPT with Threads in {128, 256, 512}, IPT >= 1; this batch 256 and 512 threads at N 16384 and 32768 (IPT 32 to 128)
contract.type_constraints: fp32 and bf16 (bf16 widened to fp32 for the bracket image), int32 indices from the striped tile position
contract.nan_behavior: not supported by N6 (the bracket image is finite), never produced by the focus set
contract.tie_break_support: prefer_smaller_index by the warp-redundant rank (not measured in this batch, not_guaranteed only)

correctness_notes: Block-size sweep of the unchanged wave 1 adapter B1_n6b at 256 and 512 threads in one lock section on umbriel-b200-020 (card _2 of the variant, the first card measured 256 threads against B1_n6), against B1_idx at the same block size, not_guaranteed only. 24 shapes (bf16 and fp32, N 16384 and 32768, k 16, 64, 256, two block sizes), oracle 13 cases per shape for variant and control, all passed, no failed or unsupported cells. The 256-thread N 32768 cells reproduce the verified B1_n6 chain (bf16 k 16 20035 against B1_idx 16850 here, 19177 against 16352 through B1_n6 in the verifier's batches, fp32 14661 against 15516). Written by opt-N8 for the N8 block-size study, the adapter source is opt-B1's.

low_level: Registers and spills: at 512 threads (128-register cap) N6b holds 128 registers with 0 spill at N 16384 (IPT 32) and 128 with 3852 to 3856 bytes of spill, 424 bytes of stack, 229 to 230 STL and 733 to 735 LDL at N 32768 (IPT 64); at 256 threads 255 registers with 0 spill at N 16384 (IPT 64) and 255 with 7276 bytes of spill, 632 bytes of stack, 330 STL and 1489 LDL at N 32768 (IPT 128). Halving the tile per thread halves the spill but does not remove it: the per-item image plus the per-bucket tracking state fill 128 registers at 64 items per thread as they filled 255 at 128.

The control B1_idx at 512 threads: 64 registers at N 16384 and 100 to 103 at N 32768, 0 spill (40 bytes for fp32 N 16384), against 128 and 248 to 250 at 256 threads. SASS sizes: N6b 15216 to 8384 instructions (bf16 N 16384 latency kernel, 256 to 512 threads), 32208 to 17088 (N 32768); B1_idx 5344 to 3056 and 10296 to 5592.

Occupancy in the throughput regime: N6b 1 block per SM at both block sizes and both N (255 and 128 registers), so the 512-thread form runs 16 warps per SM against 8; B1_idx 2 blocks per SM at N 16384 (both sizes) and 1 at N 32768.
algorithmic: N6b at 512 against 256 threads, latency (ratio 256 over 512), on the card's node umbriel-b200-020 and, after the slash, on umbriel-b200-068 (verify-N8's rerun of the same binaries, batch state/results/verify-N8/B1_n6b_vs_B1_idx_n8_vn8_f_20261025_154905.json): bf16 N 16384 1.05x/0.99x, 1.09x/1.06x, 1.19x/1.18x at k 16, 64, 256 (5838, 7404, 9938 against 6102, 8099, 11837 on 020; 5865, 7428, 9937 against 5789, 7888, 11703 on 068); bf16 N 32768 1.08x/1.03x, 1.03x/0.99x, 1.02x/1.01x; fp32 N 16384 0.96x/0.89x, 1.06x/1.03x, 1.16x/1.14x; fp32 N 32768 0.99x/0.94x, 0.91x/0.89x, 0.88x/0.89x. Throughput is node invariant (24 of 24 cells within 1 percent): 1.14x, 1.19x, 1.24x at bf16 N 16384, 1.21x, 1.08x, 1.05x at bf16 N 32768, 1.09x, 1.15x, 1.24x at fp32 N 16384, 1.15x, 1.03x, 0.98x at fp32 N 32768. NODE DEPENDENT: the k 16 latency gain of 512 threads at N 16384 (1.05x bf16 and 0.96x fp32 on 020) is a tie (0.99x) or an 11 percent loss (0.89x) on 068, because the 255-register 256-thread N6b kernels run 3.5 to 6.4 percent faster there (5789 against 6102, 5403 against 5752, 18754 against 20035) while the 512-thread kernels run 2.1 to 2.8 percent faster and B1_idx within 2.9 percent; the card reproduces on 020 within 0.11 percent (verify-N8, 16:05Z), so this is a stable node difference of the 255-register kernels, not drift. HOLDS ON BOTH NODES: the 512-thread throughput gains at N 16384 (1.08x to 1.24x) and bf16 N 32768 (1.05x to 1.21x), the k 64 and k 256 latency gains at N 16384 (1.03x to 1.19x), and the N 32768 latency verdicts (512 threads 0.88x to 1.08x, within 8 percent of 256 for bf16, 6 to 12 percent behind for fp32 k 64 and 256). The 512-thread form helps N6b where it does not spill (N 16384) and does little or harm at N 32768, where the remaining 3.9 KB of spill at 128 registers is a larger share of a 64-item sweep than 7.3 KB was of a 128-item sweep.

Against B1_idx at the same block size, latency ratio B1_idx over N6b: at 256 threads 1.48x, 1.16x, 0.93x (bf16 N 16384, k 16, 64, 256), 0.84x, 0.66x, 0.66x (bf16 N 32768), 1.58x, 1.35x, 1.17x (fp32 N 16384), 1.06x, 1.03x, 1.00x (fp32 N 32768); at 512 threads 1.30x, 1.07x, 0.90x, then 0.73x, 0.55x, 0.53x, then 1.26x, 1.17x, 1.06x, then 0.79x, 0.69x, 0.64x. N6b's N 16384 k 16 cells are new (the N6 cards had N 1024, 4096 and 32768): 1.48x and 1.58x over B1_idx at 256 threads, the largest N6 margin measured so far, kept at 1.30x and 1.26x when both run at 512 threads. At N 32768 the 512-thread B1_idx (13507 bf16, 11800 fp32 at k 16) is 1.27x to 1.9x ahead of every N6b form, so the block size settles the N 32768 question for B1_idx and not for N6. On umbriel-b200-068 the same margins read 1.54x and 1.65x at 256 threads and 1.29x and 1.26x at 512 threads (verify-N8), so the N 16384 k 16 headline of N6b holds on both nodes while the block size verdict at that cell does not.

Block size recommendation for N6b: at N 16384, 512 threads for throughput at every k (1.08x to 1.24x, both nodes) and for latency from k 64 (1.03x to 1.19x, both nodes); at k 16 the 512-thread latency is a tie or a loss (bf16 1.05x on umbriel-b200-020 and 0.99x on umbriel-b200-068, fp32 0.96x and 0.89x), so 256 threads for the latency of k 16. At N 32768: 256 threads for fp32 latency (512 is 0.88x to 0.99x), either for bf16 (within 8 percent, both behind B1_idx at 512 threads by 1.3x to 1.9x on both nodes), 512 for throughput (0.98x to 1.21x). The N 32768 register problem of N6 (B1 report section 8) is not solved by the block size, it needs the shared-memory resident rest or the recompute of the bf16 image that the report lists.
negative: The k 16 latency gain of 512 threads at N 16384 is node dependent (1.05x and 0.96x on umbriel-b200-020, 0.99x and 0.89x on umbriel-b200-068): the card's first recommendation range of 1.05x to 1.24x at N 16384 excluded its own fp32 k 16 cell (0.96x) and is replaced by the per-regime statement above.

512 threads do not remove N6b's spill at N 32768 (3.9 KB against 7.3 KB), and fp32 N 32768 gets slower (0.88x to 0.99x): the 128-register cap at 16 warps leaves less per thread for the image and the trackers than 255 did at 8 warps, and the extra spill traffic of 16 warps competes for the same L1.
N6b at 512 threads loses throughput to B1_idx at 512 threads at every cell (0.58x to 0.92x), where B1_idx's own gain from the block size is larger (1.27x to 1.44x at N 32768).
surprises: The k 16 cells at N 16384 show the largest N6 advantage of the study (1.48x bf16, 1.58x fp32 over B1_idx at 256 threads), between the N 4096 figures (1.18x and 1.23x in the verified card) and the N 32768 losses; one bracket pass plus a finish against two or three radix passes pays most where the sweep is long but the registers still hold the tile.

fp32 N 32768 is the one shape where 512 threads make N6b slower although the spill halves: the sweep per pass halves too, so the spill loads per sweep item stay, and the 16-warp block pays a 44-cycle barrier (T11) per pass boundary.
open_questions: Harness 0.4 fit caveat (verify-N8, confirmed and fixed by the evaluation engineer in harness 0.6): 14 of 24 latency cells of the rerun move by more than 3 percent under a 1 to 8 fit of the recorded chain minima (the chain of 16 leaves L1 at N 16384 and 32768), so the absolute nets of this card await harness 0.6; the card against rerun comparison and the 512 against 256 ratios are between cells with the same exposure.
N6b at 1024 threads (IPT 32 at N 32768, 64-register cap) was not measured; B1_idx and B3 at 1024 threads are in the N8 block-size batch.

Whether N6b's N 16384 k 16 margin (1.48x and 1.58x) survives the throughput regime at a matched block size: at 256 threads N6b is 0.86x to 0.87x of B1_idx in throughput (1 block per SM against 2), at 512 threads 0.91x to 0.92x.
